channel.title: Anthropic News
channel.description: Posts from anthropic.com/news, built from the site's sitemap, and from the X accounts in x-accounts.txt. Unofficial.

item.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
item.description: Today Anthropic, PBC announced the closing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a public offering price of $83.00 per share, including the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common stock from Anthropic at the initial public offering price.

item.title: Anthropic prices initial public offering
item.description: Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: You can now opt into more frequent builds of Claude Desktop on Windows and Mac.
item.description:
You can now opt into more frequent builds of Claude Desktop on Windows and Mac.
Switch to the Latest release channel in Settings > Desktop app. You'll get fixes and improvements faster, but these builds can be less reliable than Stable, which stays the default.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Check out Code Mode, a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools. Claude writes scri…
item.description:
Check out Code Mode, a new, experimental way for Claude Code to work with tools. Claude writes scripts that chain your tools together in sophisticated ways, and it can answer you while long commands are still running.
Opt in with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 http://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Platforms can offer Claude without building their own metering or invoicing. They decide who pays o…
item.description:
Platforms can offer Claude without building their own metering or invoicing. They decide who pays on each request and can understand usage by customer.
Customers can draw down an existing Anthropic commitment or pay as they go, and see spend by platform.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Linked billing is live today in beta with Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield…
item.description:
Linked billing is live today in beta with Asana, ClickHouse, Factory, Gumloop, Harness, Higgsfield AI, Kilo Code, Linear, Major, Mintlify, Niteshift, Omni, OpenArt, Railway, Ramp, Runlayer, Tessera, Tines and Warp.
To add support or learn more: https://claude.com/blog/linked-billing-on-claude-platform

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Linked billing is now in beta on the Claude Platform.
item.description:
Linked billing is now in beta on the Claude Platform.
Now users of tools like Factory, Linear, and Ramp can pay for Claude API usage through their Claude Platform organization, without sharing an API key.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests…
item.description:
Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests, benchmarks, and end-to-end runs, are now cheap.
Here’s how the Claude Code team thinks about verification: https://claude.dev/blog/how-the-claude-code-team-thinks-about-verification/

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Working in a terminal? The Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace.
item.description:
Working in a terminal? The Xcode plugin is now in the official Claude Code plugin marketplace.
Claude can use it to build, run, and test your app, render SwiftUI previews, and search developer docs.
/plugin install xcode@claude-plugins-official

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Available today in Claude Code on desktop (macOS, Xcode 27.1 or later).
item.description:
Available today in Claude Code on desktop (macOS, Xcode 27.1 or later).
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop-ios-simulator#test-your-app-on-an-iphone-duo

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Claude Code on desktop now supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta).
item.description:
Claude Code on desktop now supports iPhone Duo in the iOS simulator (public beta).
You can run your app on Duo next to your conversation and Claude can fold and unfold the device to test each layout.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Update to the latest version of the desktop app to try it. Themes work in local sessions in the des…
item.description:
Update to the latest version of the desktop app to try it. Themes work in local sessions in the desktop app today, support for cloud sessions is coming soon.
If you'd like to write one yourself, check out the docs:
https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/interface#put-a-backdrop-behind-the-conversation

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: You can now build custom themes for Claude Code on desktop with mods! Change the colors, add an ani…
item.description:
You can now build custom themes for Claude Code on desktop with mods! Change the colors, add an animated background, and make it your own.
Just tell Claude how you want it to look, or get started quickly with the theme-examples plugin. We'd love to see what you make!

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Project settings and local folder access are simpler now too. It's all on web and desktop, and the…
item.description:
Project settings and local folder access are simpler now too. It's all on web and desktop, and the latest mobile app has the new design.
Projects is in public beta on Pro and Max. If you don’t have it yet, you can join the waitlist!
https://claude.com/form/projects

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: Artifacts are easier to find again too.
item.description:
Artifacts are easier to find again too.
The threads panel now has a row at the top with the ones you recently opened, updated, or pinned. Each thread also shows thumbnails of its own artifacts, which you can turn off in the view settings.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: /btw and /fork work in projects now too.
item.description:
/btw and /fork work in projects now too.
If something else comes up while you're working, /btw gives it its own thread so your current one stays on topic.
And if you want to try a different approach, /fork starts a new thread from the one you're in.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: You can also set a reminder on any thread, or just ask Claude to remind you.
item.description:
You can also set a reminder on any thread, or just ask Claude to remind you.
The thread moves out of your way until then. When it's time, it moves back and Claude brings it up in the project chat.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: You can now share an individual thread as a read-only link with anyone who's signed in to Claude.
item.description:
You can now share an individual thread as a read-only link with anyone who's signed in to Claude.
Open the thread's menu and pick Share! Threads that had access to your computer can't be shared.

item.title: @ClaudeDevs: We've made some big updates to Projects in Claude Code!
item.description:
We've made some big updates to Projects in Claude Code!
In a project, Claude coordinates your tasks across parallel threads. The coordinator is now much more proactive. It answers your questions in the project chat and gives you updates on the status of your ongoing threads.

item.description:
Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents is now in private beta.
You can host the agent harness, sandboxes, and session history, in your own cloud or on-premises, and choose where requests to Claude are sent.

item.title: Physicist Christopher Stubbs joins Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust
item.description: Dr. Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist and former Dean of Science at Harvard University, has joined Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust. He brings to the Trust decades of scientific expertise across observational cosmology and precision measurement. He has also advised the US government on national security and arms control. “I am honored to join Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust and to help the company deliver on its public benefit mission,” said Stubbs. “I use AI tools in my research every day and see what they make possible, and as an educator I have confronted some of the hard questions they raise. As a grandfather, I want to help ensure that AI is developed and deployed for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Stubbs is the Samuel C. Moncher Professor of Physics and of Astronomy at Harvard, where he served as Dean of Science from 2018 to 2024. In 1998, as a member of the High-Z Supernova Search Team, he helped discover the accelerating expansion of the universe, work that later earned the team the Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics. He was also the inaugural project scientist for what is now the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which started a 10-year survey of the southern sky in June. One of its aims is to study the accelerating expansion he helped discover. More recently, he’s written about how to keep AI-assisted research reproducible when models can give different answers to the same question. He’s a member of JASON, an independent group of scientists who have advised the US government on defense and technology since 1960. "When Chris found evidence that the universe was expanding at a rate no one expected, he and his team followed the data even when it went against the prevailing wisdom of the field. As AI starts to transform how science itself is done, Chris’s intellectual honesty, rigor, and commitment to the truth are the values we want shaping the future of this technology, and I’m grateful he’s bringing his deep expertise to the Trust," said Daniela Amodei, Co-founder and President of Anthropic. Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation, which means we’re structured to balance commercial growth with our public benefit purpose. The Trust exists to help us hold that balance over the long term. It has the authority to appoint a majority of Anthropic’s board, and Trustees advise the board and our leadership on critical decisions, particularly those involving risks and societal impacts of AI. This week we published our first Public Benefit Report [link], a public account of how we’re working toward our mission and where we’re falling short. The Trustees helped define the five mission pillars it measures us against, and the report closes with their assessment of our progress to date. Subject to stockholder approval, we’ve also committed to setting aside a portion of Anthropic’s shares to Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. “Anthropic's Public Benefit Report sets out what we’re all working toward: helping the world build powerful AI safely, and making sure the technology drives advances that meaningfully improve people’s lives and society as a whole,” added Neil Buddy Shah, Chair of the Long-Term Benefit Trust. “Both goals depend on a deep understanding of frontier science and leading with integrity. Not only has Chris worked on some of the hardest problems in science, but he has consistently been a high-integrity leader of large, complex, collaborative scientific endeavors across academia, government, and the national laboratories. That will be of great value to the Trust as we support Anthropic in developing AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.” Stubbs, the Trust’s first physicist, joins Shah, national security expert Richard Fontaine, and former Federal Reserve Chair Ben Bernanke. Trustees are independent of the company’s management and investors.
